headline: Net interest margin narrows as loan book shrinks post-sale
summary_short: Q2 2026 diluted EPS was $0.29, down 9.4% y/y and down sharply from Q1's loan-sale-inflated $1.54, as net interest income fell to $333M on a smaller Private Education Loan book while non-interest income normalized to $68M from Q1's $185M.
summary_long: Net interest income fell to $333M (-12% q/q, -12% y/y) as average Private Education Loans outstanding declined following the March 2026 seasoned loan sale; net interest margin compressed to 4.75% from 5.31% a year ago as asset yields fell faster than funding costs. Provision for credit losses eased to $126M from $149M y/y on an $11M negative provision tied to the $420 million Q2 loan sale to SLM's strategic partner. Diluted EPS of $0.29 was down from $0.32 y/y and far below Q1's loan-sale-boosted $1.54. Cash fell to $4,588M from $5,157M q/q as deposits declined. The Company's FY2026 guidance calls for EPS of $3.10-$3.20, Private Education Loan origination growth of 12%-14%, net charge-offs of $365-385M, and non-interest expenses of $750-780M.

drivers.explanation: Company frames Q2 as 'stable earnings performance' with continued originations growth, citing disciplined funding, expense, and capital-management decisions offsetting lower net interest income.
Q/q drop driven mainly by non-interest income falling to $68M from Q1's $185M, since Q1 booked outsized gains on the $3.33B seasoned loan sale versus Q2's smaller $420M sale ($15M gain).

Q1 2026 net income of $308M was inflated by a $3.33B loan sale generating large gains and an $11M net negative provision; Q2's $126M provision expense and smaller $420M loan sale return results to a lower run rate.
Y/y decline reflects lower net interest income on a smaller loan book, primarily due to the March 2026 seasoned loan sale reducing average Private Education Loans outstanding by $1.4 billion.
The $500 million of short-term Senior Notes due November 2026 was tendered for and discharged in May 2026, funded by issuing $500 million of new unsecured Senior Notes (now classified long-term).
Rose q/q as the new $500 million unsecured Senior Notes issued in May 2026 replaced the discharged short-term notes; down y/y on overall lower borrowings.

Q/q decline is roughly consistent with deposits falling from $20,525M to $19,895M; y/y increase reflects liquidity built from loan-sale proceeds as loans held for investment fell from $21.16B to $19.53B.
Reflects the $200 million accelerated share repurchase completed in June 2026, which retired 9.3 million shares in total at an average price of $21.59.
Growth driven by H1 2026 net income of $366M, partially offset by $301M of share repurchases and $57M of common/preferred dividends declared in the period.
